name: Sohar International Bank
founded: 2007 (established 4 March 2007 as Bank Sohar SAOG; commercial operations from 9 April 2007; merged by incorporation with HSBC Bank Oman SAOG on 17 August 2023)
ownership_summary: Listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange. At 30 Jun 2026 the main holders were Royal Court Affairs 19.4%, Dhofar International Development & Investment Co SAOG 13.0%, The Seventh Moon Investment LLC 6.4%, Neptune National Investments LLC 5.5% and Western Sea Investments LLC 5.4%; others 50.3%. In August 2026 a rights issue of 1,058,759,403 shares at Baisa 141 raised OMR 149.3m gross, taking paid-up capital to OMR 849.7m (7,676,005,673 shares). Post-rights-issue holdings have not been published.
government_link: Yes. Royal Court Affairs holds 19.4% (30 Jun 2026). The chairman is CEO of a government-owned investment fund company (FY2025 annual report). The CBO designated the bank a Domestic Systemically Important Bank in March 2025 (S1, S2).
group_structure: A single bank with an Islamic window, Sohar Islamic (licensed 30 Apr 2013; 21 branches at 30 Jun 2026). It has a branch in Riyadh (SAMA approval Oct 2023; inaugurated 2025) and a Hong Kong Asia Pacific representative office (HKMA approval Apr 2026, CBO approval May 2026, opened Sep 2026). HSBC Bank Oman SAOG was merged in by incorporation on 17 Aug 2023. The only subsidiary disclosed is Sohar International Netting SPV Limited (Cayman Islands), which was not yet operating at 31 Dec 2025. Two acquisitions are pending, with no completion found: up to 55% of Neo Group Limited KSA, a CMA-licensed asset management and advisory firm (in-principle CBO approval reported Dec 2025), and up to 100% of Insurance House LLC ('Bima'), a digital insurance platform (non-binding offer, Aug 2025). A proposed merger with Ahli Bank (LOI April 2025) was put on hold in June 2025 when regulatory approvals were not received.

subsidiaries.name: Sohar International Netting SPV Limited (Cayman Islands)
subsidiaries.activity: Treasury netting SPV for derivative counterparties. It had not started operations at 31 Dec 2025.

footprint: At 30 Jun 2026: 55 commercial banking branches and 21 Islamic branches in Oman, plus one branch in Riyadh, KSA. The bank reports operating in 2 countries. A Hong Kong representative office (Asia Pacific Office) opened in September 2026 (S1, S12).
customer_segments: Retail (personal banking, youth and minor accounts, Be Zahiya and Zahiya Plus for women), Premier (Premier Lite), Wealth Management (HNWI), Private Banking (UHNWI, family offices, non-residents), SME, corporate, government, financial institutions, Islamic (Sohar Islamic).
business_lines: Segments (H1 2026 note 33): Retail Banking, covering Retail & Premier Banking and Wealth Management (HNWI advisory). Wholesale Banking, covering Corporate Banking, Investment Banking (DCM advisory, custody, funds management and the proprietary portfolio), Government, International Banking & Private Banking (foreign investors, family offices, non-residents, UHNWI) and Global Markets. Islamic Banking (Sohar Islamic). KSA Branch (wholesale). In 2025 the bank set up a Government Investment Advisory unit (S1, S2).

capabilities.wealth_summary: Sohar International runs wealth in three tiers. Premier Lite needs a minimum salary of OMR 700. Sohar Wealth Management, launched in 2019, needs a deposit or investments of OMR 30,000, or a salary of OMR 3,000 a month; it offers a dedicated RM, 'personalized wealth advisory', a Signature debit card and 'access to investment products'. Private Banking for UHNWI, family offices and non-residents sits in a separate International Banking & Private Banking unit. The investment shelf on the site is narrow: fixed and structured deposits, Government Development Bonds and FX. No mutual fund shelf, brokerage or in-app investing was found, and the FSA register shows no brokerage licence. The bank is FSA-licensed as investment manager, portfolio manager, custodian and issuer of structured instruments. It reports off-balance-sheet 'assets under management' of OMR 1,805m (30 Jun 2026), a figure that includes custody. In September 2026 it opened a Hong Kong office. At the same time it signed an exclusive deal to market E-Fund's (China) investment products in Oman and the region through its Asset Management and Origination & Placement businesses, and an MoU with alternatives manager Templewater on investment opportunities and co-investments for eligible clients. A planned 55% acquisition of Neo Group KSA (CMA-licensed asset management and advisory) had not been completed in any source found.

segments.name: Sohar Wealth Management
segments.eligibility: Minimum deposit OMR 30,000, or investments of OMR 30,000 or more, or monthly salary OMR 3,000 or more

private_banking.detail: The International Banking & Private Banking unit, led by Aziz Al Jahdhami, provides personalised solutions to family offices, non-residents and UHNWI (note 33). The FY2025 annual report says the private banking proposition 'advanced into a more integrated and relationship-led ecosystem' for HNW and UHNW clients, combining wealth advisory, lifestyle privileges and multi-generational legacy planning, and lists private banking as a 2026 priority. In 2019 the bank signed an alliance with EFG International that gave Omani clients access to a Swiss private banking relationship; its current status is unknown.

asset_management.detail: This is in-house, not a separate entity: 'funds management' sits in the Investment Banking segment. FSA licences cover Investment Manager, Portfolio Management, Fund Administration and Custodian. Fiduciary 'assets under management' (including custody) were OMR 1,805m at 30 Jun 2026. In Sep 2026 E-Fund named the bank its exclusive partner to market E-Fund products through its 'Asset Management and Origination & Placement businesses'. Pending: up to 55% of Neo Group Limited KSA (CMA-licensed asset management and advisory). No in-house fund names were found.

brokerage.detail: The FSA register does not list Brokerage among Sohar International's licensed securities activities. No brokerage or trading service was found on sib.om.

digital_investing.detail: 2025 mobile app enhancements cover goal-based savings, bill payments, recurring transfers and Google, Apple and Samsung Pay. An Open Banking API platform was launched in 2025. No investing feature was found in the app or on the site.

advisory.detail: Wealth Management offers a dedicated RM and a 'personalized wealth advisory service'. The bank holds an FSA Investment Advice & Research licence. A Government Investment Advisory unit was set up in 2025 for institutional clients.

discretionary.detail: The FSA Portfolio Management licence and the fiduciary note's 'portfolio and investment management' indicate managed portfolios, but no client-facing discretionary mandate product is described.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: None found on sib.om or in the annual report.

funds_platform.detail: Wealth clients get 'access to investment products' (not specified). E-Fund products are to be marketed under the Sep 2026 partnership (announced). The 2019 EFG International alliance gave access to EFG's product shelf. No live third-party fund list was found.

structured_products.detail: Structured Deposits are listed on the Wealth 'Global Market' page. The bank holds an FSA licence as Issuer of Structured Instruments. Terms are not published.

private_markets.detail: MoU with Templewater (Asia/GCC alternatives manager), 10 Sep 2026, covering investment opportunities for eligible Sohar clients and potential co-investments. It is not yet a product.

islamic_wealth.detail: Sohar Islamic has 21 branches with Islamic deposits, financing and cards. No Shariah-compliant investment or wealth product was found.

opportunities: The 2026 outlook says it will 'strengthen its Private Banking proposition' with 'personalised advisory, tailored wealth solutions, and exclusive lifestyle and investment services' (S2 p.28).
The investment shelf on the site is narrow (deposits, structured deposits, Government Development Bonds, FX), and no app investing, model portfolios or fund platform was found (S10, S2).
It is actively adding investment-product partners: E-Fund exclusive distribution and the Templewater alternatives MoU (Sep 2026) (S12).
API-first posture: an Open Banking platform with fintech integrations launched in 2025, and the CTDO's remit includes fintech partnerships (S2).
Fast balance-sheet growth: assets +12% and loans +21% in H1 2026, with fresh capital (OMR 149.3m rights issue in Aug 2026) (S1, S6).

open_items: Lead check: the HSBC Oman integration is confirmed. The merger by incorporation with HSBC Bank Oman SAOG was completed on 17 Aug 2023 (S2 note 1).

Lead check: 2025–2026 mergers. No merger has been completed. The April 2025 Ahli Bank merger proposal was put on hold in June 2025 because regulatory approvals were not received.
